newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Profit-taking seen in Quantum.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Profit-taking seen in Quantum.

text.p: A few call options on shares of Quantum Corp were busy Wednesday as investors apparently took profits as the stock rallied on strong earnings.
By 1100 CST/1700 GMT, Quantum shares were up 2-7/8 at 36, just off their session high of 36-1/8, which was a new 52-week high. More than 7.2 million shares traded.

Late Tuesday, the disk drive maker reported fiscal third quarter earnings of $0.71 per share compared with a loss of $0.05 in the year ago quarter and analyst consensus expectations of earnings of $0.52 a share.
The Quantum February 35 call traded about 3,870 contracts, the March 35 call traded 1,815 and the February 30 call traded 1,045.
The most active Quantum put was the February 25, with volume of 25 contracts.
Volatilities remained high around 68, compared with an average of around 43 for the month. Volatilities had picked up over the last several days in anticipation of the earnings.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said open interest in the February 35 calls had been steadily increasing since January 10.
Schwartz said the pattern, which culminated in turnover of 1,665 contracts Tuesday, suggested growing expectations of an upside earnings surprise. Open interest through Tuesday was 4,078 contracts.
"With today's volume, I'd say there's a lot of profit-taking going on," he said.
The February 35 call was up 1/2 at 2-3/4. The February 30 call was up 1-3/4 at 6-1/4.
Schwartz added that some investors might be rolling positions out to the March 35 calls, which had open interest of just 726.
The company's comment that its revenues would see little change in the fourth quarter ending in March compared with the third quarter did not appear to concern investors.
Similar comments from some other technology companies have led to heavy selling.
Schwartz said some of the action in the March 35 calls could be market makers using that as hedge against selling February 35 calls.
Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, said the stock's intermediate term outlook was bright.
"For those with a six-month or longer time horizon, patience would likely be rewarded," he said, noting that the stock has broken out to the upside.
Quantum shares opened at 35-3/8, creating a two-point upside gap on the daily chart.

"On a near-term basis, I would be inclined to take trading profits in the stock," Nie said. "'Buy the rumor, sell the news' has been an effective strategy, more so in an anticipation of a sideways market for the near term."
